why: WebFetches third-party agent markdown from an external directory and writes it into .claude/agents/ as a supervisor with tools: * (discovery.md:83-107, 160-168) — untrusted web text becoming a privileged system prompt with all tools. subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/block-orchestrator-tools
why: Blanket write-denial for the session agent contradicts our Working Mode, which routes small tasks inline. On its own terms it is leaky: the git allowlist has no default-deny arm — push --force, reset --hard, clean -fd all fall through to exit 0 (:126-147, :167), all of which our block-dangerous-commands.sh denies — and the --no-verify test matches any '-n' substring (:138), denying innocent commits. The one good fragment, a bd create description floor (:154-161), is deferred: it would misfire on our thin idea-bead flow without an -l idea exemption, and we lack evidence thin beads cause rework.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/enforce-bead-for-supervisor
why: The gap it closes is real — nothing stops dispatching an implementer with no tracked bead — but the mechanical check needs a convention we have not mandated: a bead id field in every dispatch brief. Re-open when the execution skill's brief format requires that field; then this becomes a one-check PreToolUse:Task hook.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/enforce-sequential-dispatch
why: Three checks: the closed-bead guard (:29-35) is a genuine gap for us (closed beads are our durable rejection record with nothing preventing a re-claim) and is deferred into bead cr-ghw; the blocker check is redundant for us (bd ready --parent is dependency-truth by construction); the design-doc check presupposes the architect flow that deadlocks at this pin. Only the first survives, as cr-ghw.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/enforce-branch-before-edit
why: Enforces edits-only-in-worktrees; presupposes worktree-per-task, which we do not run — our review packages the working tree because implementers do not commit.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:hooks/block-branch-for-epic-child
why: Same worktree/branch model presupposition, and internally contradictory at the pin: it forces children onto a shared bd-{EPIC_ID} branch while the worker template creates bd-{BEAD_ID} per child and validate-completion.sh checks the remote for the per-child branch that the shared model never creates. Also half-broken: primary detection reads a .conversation_context field the event does not supply.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/validate-completion
why: TCP's flagship gate, and the strongest single reason to distrust the framework's enforcement claims: it reads .agent_transcript_path — not a documented SubagentStop field — and explicitly approves-and-exits when it is empty (:7, :11), so it fails open; its block shape ({"decision":"block"}) is also undocumented for SubagentStop. Even granting the plumbing, it checks only bookkeeping (worktree exists, tree clean, branch pushed, status inreview, response length) and never test evidence — 'Tests: pass' is a literal template string the worker fills in. Our verification-before-completion is a strictly better specification; the mechanizable subset (epic-close) goes to cr-ghw instead.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/validate-epic-close
why: The shipped implementation is a no-op: it reads a CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT env var Claude Code never sets and exits 0 (:8, :11), and its own test drives it the same wrong way (tests/test-validate-epic-close.sh:37) — a suite validating the mock. But CHECK 2 (deny closing an epic with open children) is exactly the jq check our execution skill states as prose (execution/SKILL.md:89-93); deferred into bead cr-ghw as a stdin-driven reimplementation with a named override. CHECK 1 (merged-PR required) is rejected — it would deadlock our conservative commit/push authority.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/log-dispatch-prompt
why: The single most valuable mechanism in TCP: PostToolUse:Task auto-appends the dispatch prompt onto the bead as a DISPATCH comment (:30-37) — zero agent cooperation, and it closes our real gap that execution briefs live in gitignored scratchpad and are unrecoverable after a workstream closes. Deferred into bead cr-n0v because it carries a policy question the user must settle (a hook writing to bd vs conservative authority) plus truncation/disclosure design; reimplement, never copy.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/memory-capture
why: Right idea (frictionless capture), poor implementation: the comment body is reconstructed by regex over the shell command string (:28) — quoted ids, heredocs, and -m forms silently capture nothing — and the tag vocabulary is hardcoded Swift/AppKit terms (:57-60) from its origin project. The recall tool advertises an 'investigation' type this hook can never produce. Its provenance idea (source + bead fields, docs/memory-architecture.md:50-54) was adopted now as the optional Source: line in project/learnings.md. Re-open capture automation only if manual learnings capture demonstrably loses entries; any rebuild targets our learnings.md format.

subject: The-Claude-Protocol:hook:templates/hooks/session-start
why: The surfacing half of their knowledge loop is what our write-only learnings.md lacks, and SessionStart stdout genuinely reaches the model. Deferred into bead cr-iqu: last 3-5 learnings titles, a dirty-tree warning, and a stale-beads line added to bd-prime.sh, hard-capped. Rejected within it: worktree cleanup (no worktree model) and gh pr list (a network call every session).

why: PreToolUse plain-text stdout is debug-logged, never added to model context — the hook cannot do its job as wired; and the content it would inject is already mandated by our execution skill's claim step.
